THE NATIONAL BANK OF RWANDA,

Pursuant to Law n° 48/2017 of 23/09/2017 governing the National Bank of Rwanda as
amended to date, especially in Articles 6, 6 bis, 8 and 9;

Pursuant to regulation n° 28/2019 of 09/09/2019 relating to publication of financial
statements and other disclosures by banks, especially in articles 8, 9,10, 12, and 15;

Pursuant to regulation n°47/2022 of 02/06/2022 on publication of financial statements and
other disclosures by insurers, especially in Articles 10, 11, 12,13, 14, 15 and 16;

Pursuant to regulation n° 60/2023 of 27/03/2023 determining prudential norms for deposit-
taking microfinance institutions, especially in Articles 29, 30 and 31;

Pursuant to regulation n° 65/04/2023 of 25/04/2023 governing non-deposit taking financial
services providers, especially in article 33;

Pursuant to guidelines n° 2600/2023- 00036[616] of 29/11/2023 on climate-related and
environmental financial risks for regulated Financial Institutions, especially in Articles 15, 16,
17, 18, 19 and 20;

Having noted that the transparency achieved by public disclosures and reporting of
sustainability related financial information by Financial Institutions is expected to hold
financial institutions accountable for their actions to their investors, lenders, creditors and
other stakeholders for their actions in addressing sustainability-related risks and
opportunities;

Given that IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards introduced a mechanism for achieving
such disclosures and reporting;

Recognizing our collective efforts to building resilience and greening the financial sector;

ISSUES THE FOLLOWING GUIDELINES

CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article One: The purpose of these guidelines
The purpose of these guidelines is to:

(a) establish the sustainability-related financial information disclosure and reporting
requirements by Financial Institutions.

BNR RESTRICTED
Page 3 of 24
(b) provide additional requirements to those provided by the guidelines N° 2600/2023 -
00036 [616] of 29/11/2023 on Climate-Related and Environmental Financial Risks
Management for Financial Institutions, specifically on:

(i) disclosure and reporting of sustainability-related financial information.

(ii) implementation of adoption deadlines; and

(iii) guidance for compliance with the provisions of Chapter IV of the 2023 Guidelines.

(iv) reinforcement of the requirements of Chapter IV of the 2023 Guidelines and explicitly
mandate adherence to said chapter.

(c) require Financial Institutions to align their governance, strategy, and risk management
reporting and disclosures concerning their sustainability-related risks with these
guidelines, including the specified phases that lead to compliance with IFRS Sustainability
Disclosures.

Article 2: Interpretations
In these guidelines:

(a) “Central Bank” means the National Bank of Rwanda;

(b) "2023 Guidelines" means Guidelines N° 2600/2023 - 00036 [616] of 29/11/2023 on
Climate-Related and Environmental Financial Risks Management for Financial Institutions.

(c) “Climate-related risks and opportunities" means the potential risks and opportunities
that may arise from climate change or from efforts to mitigate climate change, their related
impacts and their economic and financial consequences;

(d) “Environmental-related financial risks and opportunities" means financial risks and
opportunities posed by the exposure of Financial Institutions to activities that may
potentially cause or be affected by environmental degradation (such as air pollution, water
pollution and scarcity of fresh water, land contamination and diversity desertification,
biodiversity loss, and deforestation) and the loss of ecosystem services;

(e) “Financial Institutions” include a bank, a deposit-taking microfinance institution, an
insurer, a pension scheme and a non-deposit-taking financial service provider that grants
or provides loans or similar services or products, if and to the extent that such reporting
entity is regulated by the Central Bank;

(f) “IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards” means the sustainability standards
developed by ISSB;

(g) “IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial
Information (IFRS $1)” means the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards that
specifies:

(i) how a reporting entity prepares and reports its sustainability-related financial
disclosures, including general requirements for the content and presentation of those

BNR RESTRICTED
Page 4 of 24
disclosures so that the information disclosed is useful to users in making decisions relating

to providing resources to the reporting entity (the general requirements), and

(ii) the requirements for identifying and disclosing information about a reporting entity’s
sustainability-related risks and opportunities (the core requirements).

(h) “IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures (IFRS $2)” means the IFRS Sustainability
Disclosure Standard that specifies the disclosures required by a reporting entity about its
climate-related risks and opportunities that are useful to primary users of general purpose
financial reports in making decisions relating to providing resources to the reporting entity;

(i) “International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)” means the standards developed
by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and the _ International
Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB);

(j) “Sustainability-related risks and opportunities” means the potential risks and
opportunities that may arise from sustainability topics, their related impacts and their
economic and financial consequences;

(k) “Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)" means a global
organisation formed to develop a set of recommended climate-related disclosures that
companies and Financial Institutions can use to better inform investors, shareholders and
the public of their climate-related financial risks;

Article 3: Scope of Application
These guidelines apply to Financial Institutions as defined in the 2023 Guidelines.
Article 4: Application

(1) These guidelines will be implemented in phases in consideration of the specific tiers of
Financial Institutions as defined in the 2023 Guidelines and the need for Financial
Institutions to develop the prerequisite capacity and capability within the detailed
timelines specified in these guidelines.

(2) The Central Bank shall provide implementation guidance and manuals to assist Financial
Institutions in their specific sectors to implement the provisions of these guidelines
effectively. The implementation guidance and manuals provide better practices and
detailed examples of integrating sustainability-related risks into traditional risk
management frameworks.

(3) The implementation guidance and manuals also provide examples of better-practice
disclosures to help institutions transition towards meeting the requirements of IFRS Sl and
IFRS S2.

(4) Unless explicitly stated, these guidelines do not rescind any requirements in the 2023
Guidelines.

CHAPTER II: ENHANCEMENT OF CHAPTER IV OF THE 2023 GUIDELINES
Article 5: Overview of reporting and disclosure requirements

(1) Chapter IV of the 2023 Guidelines requires that, in the interest of enhanced transparency,
Financial Institutions develop a suitable approach for disclosing climate-related and
environmental financial information. It further requires that each institution at a minimum,
aligns its climate-related and environmental financial disclosures with the detailed TCFD's
recommendations, as well as the requirements of IFRS S1 and S2.

(2) The IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards supersede the TCFD recommendations.
Consequently, these guidelines withdraw and rescinds the requirements included in the
2023 Guidelines regarding reporting and disclosure requirements to be aligned with the
TCFD recommendations. It also withdraws the Annex 1 of the 2023 Guidelines.

(3) These guidelines set out requirements for reporting and disclosing sustainability-related
financial information (including climate and environmental-related financial information).

(4) Consistent with the requirements of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, in disclosing
and reporting under these guidelines, Financial Institutions must include the following:

(a) governance frameworks;
(b) strategic decision-making processes;
(c) risk management systems, and
(d) metrics and targets.
Article 6: Phasing-in of reporting and disclosure requirements

(1) The requirements of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards will be phased, over a period
appropriate to ensure that all stakeholders’ needs for information are balanced with the
capability and capacity of Financial Institutions to produce compliant, robust and credible
information at a reasonable cost.

(2) In alignment with the 2023 Guidelines, the financial institutions are classified in tiers as
follows:

(a) Tier |: Banks, general and life insurance and public pension; UMWALIMU SACCO;

(b) Tier Il: deposit-taking microfinance companies, captive insurers, micro insurers, private
pension schemes;

(c) Tier Ill: Non-deposit-taking financial service providers, MUGANGA SACCOs, Mutual
Insurers and Health Maintenance Organizations (HMO); and

Page 6 of 24
(d) Tier IV: Umurenge SACCOs and Non Umurenge SACCOs. In case of consolidation of
Umurenge SACCOs to District SACCOs, this timeline will apply to District SACCOs.

(3) The implementation of reporting requirements in these guidelines for Tier |, Tier I&Ill, and
Tier IV Financial Institutions , starts with financial periods commencing on or after January
1, 2025; January 1, 2026; and January 1, 2027 respectively with the intention to achieve full
compliance with IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards for financial periods
commencing on or after January 1, 2028; January 1, 2029; and January 1, 2030 for Tier |,
Tier I&II] and Tier IV Financial Institutions respectively as set out in Annex A of these

guidelines.

Article 7: Reporting Requirements for Implementation of Phase 1

(1) For the purposes of compliance with Article 6(3), disclosure aligned with IFRS
Sustainability Disclosure Standards comprises compliance with IFRS S2, and those parts
of IFRS S1 necessary to be compliant with IFRS S2 (Implementation Phase 1 Reporting),
but limited as set out below:

(a) Materiality: Financial Institutions need not consider the materiality requirements in
IFRS S1 that relate to material information being obscured by immaterial information
(the obscuring requirements). The obscuring requirements of IFRS S1 explicitly require
Financial Institutions to avoid disclosing information that is not financially material
because of the risk or perceived risk that non-material information may cause
financially material information to be obscured. Financial institutions do not need to
assess whether climate-related items are below the threshold for financial materiality.

Financial Institutions that apply this relief must publish all financially material
information specified in these guidelines (entities should not omit material
information) and must ensure that information is materially correct (entities should
not misstate information).

(b) Comparative information: Financial Institutions need not disclose comparative
information in their implementation Phase 1 reporting.

(c) Governance: Financial Institutions are required to disclose their governance
procedures and plans to oversee climate-related risks and opportunities, including
progress in the formation of a dedicated team tasked with monitoring and managing
these risks. Governance responsibilities include the preparation and submission of
reports to the board and senior management.

(d) Strategy: Financial Institutions must disclose how, if at all, they have integrated

climate-related risks and climate-related opportunities into their overall business

BNR RESTRICTED
Page 7 of 24
strategy. Phase 1 Reporting does not include conducting scenario analysis and stress

testing to assess the potential financial impact of climate change;

(e) Risk Management: Financial Institutions must disclose how, if at all, they have
implemented comprehensive risk management systems that incorporate climate-
related risks into traditional risk categories, such as credit, market, operational, and
liquidity risks;

(f) Financial Disclosures: For Phase 1 Reporting, Financial Institutions need not disclose:

(i) the anticipated effects of climate-related risks and opportunities on the
institution's financial position, financial performance and cash flows over the short,
medium and long term (IFRS S2 paragraph 9(d)); and

(ii) how the Financial Institution expects its financial performance and cash flows to
change over the short, medium and long term, given its strategy to manage climate-
related risks and opportunities (IFRS S2 paragraph 16(d)).

(g) Metrics and targets: Financial Institutions must, as specified in IFRS S2, disclose
information relevant to the cross-industry metric categories, industry-based metrics
and targets set by the reporting entity. However, for the purposes of Implementation
Phase 1 Reporting, Financial Institutions should focus on internal operations first. That
is, they need not include reporting on metrics, either qualitative or quantitative, tied to
or incorporated within the reporting entity’s value chain or with other related external
parties. However, they should collect information that will be required for subsequent
phases.

(2) For paragraph (1) above, refer to Annex B of these guidelines.

(3) The disclosures set out in paragraph (1) above shall be provided in or accompany the
Integrated Report of the Financial Institution in the timeframe as required by the specific
regulations for each Financial Institution. Where an Integrated Report is not required, the
disclosures are to be provided in the annual report or in a separate report within the
periods stipulated in Article 6(3) above.

(4) Nothing in these guidelines should be construed as preventing early adoption of full IFRS
Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

Article 8: Reporting Requirements for Implementation of Phase 2

(1) For the purposes of compliance with Article 6(3), disclosure aligned with IFRS
Sustainability Disclosure Standards comprises: Compliance with the requirements of
IFRS Slas applied to environmental financial-related risks and opportunities as defined in
these guidelines, together with those other parts of IFRS Sl necessary to be compliant

BNR RESTRICTED
Page 8 of 24
with IFRS 2 (Implementation Phase 2 Reporting), in addition to the requirements for
Implementation of Phase 1, but limited as set out below:

(a) Comparative information: Financial Institutions need not disclose comparative
information in respect of those disclosures not required under Implementation Phase
1 Reporting;

(b) Governance: Financial Institutions are required to disclose their governance
procedures and plans to oversee climate-related risks and opportunities and
environmental-related risks and opportunities, including progress in the formation of a
dedicated team tasked with monitoring and managing these risks. Governance
responsibilities include the preparation and submission of reports to the board and
senior management;

(c) Strategy: Financial Institutions must disclose how, if at all, they have integrated
climate-related risks and opportunities and environmental-related risks and
opportunities into their overall business strategy. For the purposes of Implementation
Phase 2 Reporting, this does not include conducting scenario analysis and stress
testing to assess the potential financial impact of climate change;

(d) Risk Management: Financial Institutions must disclose how, if at all, they have
implemented comprehensive risk management systems that incorporate climate-
related risks and environmental-related risks into traditional risk categories, such as
credit, market, operational, and liquidity risks;

(e) Financial Disclosures: For the purposes of Implementation Phase 2 Reporting,
Financial Institutions need not disclose:

(i) the anticipated effects of climate-related risks and opportunities and
environmental-related risks and opportunities on the institution’s financial
position, financial performance and cash flows over the short, medium and long
term; and

(ii) how the Financial Institution expects its financial performance and cash flows to
change over the short, medium and long term, given its strategy to manage climate-
related risks and opportunities and environmental-related risks and opportunities.

(f) Metrics and targets: Financial Institutions must disclose information relevant to the
cross-industry metric categories, industry-based metrics and targets set by the
reporting entity. However, for the purposes of Implementation Phase 2 Reporting,
Financial Institutions should focus on internal operations first. That is, they need not
include reporting on metrics, either qualitative or quantitative, tied to or incorporated

within the reporting entity’s value chain or with other related external parties. However,
they should collect information that will be required for subsequent phase.

(2) The disclosures set out in paragraph (1) above shall be provided in or accompany the
Integrated Report of the Financial Institution in the timeframe as required by the specific
legislation published for each regulated industry. Where an Integrated Report is not
required, the disclosures are to be provided in the annual report or in a separate report
within the periods stipulated in Article 6(3) above.

Article 9: Reporting Requirements for Implementation of Phase 3

For the purposes of compliance with Article 6(3), disclosure aligned with IFRS Sustainability
Disclosure Standards comprises:

(1) Full compliance with the requirements of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards as
effective at the date of initial compliance with Implementation Phase 3, including the
transitional reliefs in those standards,

(2) Without prejudice to paragraph (1), financial institutions shall continue to apply IFRS Slas
it relates to the identification and reporting of environmental financial related risks and
opportunities.

(3) Paragraphs 1 and 2 are collectively referred to as the implementation of phase 3.

CHAPTER III: FUTURE DEVELOPMENTS
Article 10: Consideration of the ISSB Adoption Roadmap

These guidelines were developed in consideration of the ISSB Adoption Roadmap (the
Adoption Roadmap), which, as of the issue date of these guidelines, is being developed by the
ISSB Standards Steering Committee under the leadership of the Institute of Certified Public
Accountants of Rwanda (ICPAR). Financial institutions will benefit from the process, data and
transparency introduced by the implementation of the Adoption Roadmap.

Article 11: Future updates to these guidelines

(1) As described below, the Central Bank shall from time to time consider and where
appropriate amend or supplement these guidelines. However, nothing in this section will
oblige the Central Bank to make such changes, and nothing in this paragraph cedes the
Central Bank 's capacity or authority for making any amendments to any other regulator
in Rwanda, save as stipulated in Law.

The Development of the Adoption Roadmap

(2) The ISSB Standards Steering Committee will develop the Adoption Roadmap in
consultation with relevant regulators and other affected stakeholders. The objective of the
Adoption Roadmap is to provide an achievable and enforceable pathway to the credible
adoption of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in Rwanda.

(3) Consideration will be given, if appropriate, to update or supplement these guidelines to
reflect the published Adoption Roadmap when the Adoption Roadmap is published.

Verification of Sustainability-related Financial Disclosures

(4) The process for, and extent and nature of, the verification of Sustainability reporting will be
established by the authorities charged with the responsibility for audit and verification of
annual reports.

New and amended IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards

(5) As of the date of publication of these guidelines, the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure
Standards consist of two standards, IFRS Sl and IFRS S2. The ISSB is expected to issue
further standards within the foreseeable future and may amend the existing ones.
Amendments and new standards that are issued will be incorporated into the body of IFRS
Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and:

(a) Complying with the requirements of Annex A (last column) will become applicable for
Tier | Financial institutions for the latter of the following two periods:

(i) financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2028; and
(ii) financial years defined as the effective date of the new standard.

(b) Complying with the requirements of Annex A (last column) will become applicable for
Tier Il and III Financial Institutions for the latter of:

(i) financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2029; and
(ii) financial years defined as the effective date of the new standard.

(c) Complying with the requirements of Annex A (last column) will become applicable for
Tier IV Financial Institutions for the latter of:

(i) financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2030; and
(ii) financial years defined as the effective date of the new standard.

(6) The Central Bank may amend these guidelines to introduce phasing in provisions for any
amendments or new standards published by the ISSB before 1 January 2029, if and to the

CHAPTER IV: FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 12: Compliance with the provisions of these guidelines

(1) The Central Bank shall enforce compliance by Financial Institutions to the provisions of
these guidelines.

(2) Non-compliance with the provisions of these guidelines may lead to supervisory corrective
actions.

Article 13: Monitoring the implementation

(1) Financial Institutions shall implement these guidelines in phases as per Annex A of these
guidelines, demonstrating their full commitment to a structured and effective process.

(2) External Auditors, in addition to their auditing activities, shall review the implementation
of these guidelines by Financial Institutions and report any implementation challenge to
the Central Bank.

(3) The Central Bank oversees the phased implementation of these guidelines.
Article 14: Entry into force
These guidelines come into force on the date of its signature.

ANNEX B: APPLICATION IFRS SUSTAINABILITY DISCLOSURE STANDARDS

(1) During the Implementation of Phase 1, Financial Institutions are required to implement the following core aspects of IFRS S2 with those parts
of IFRS Sl necessary to be compliant with IFRS S2, with optional reliefs therefrom as specified below:

Report on Existing Governance, Risk, and Strategy in Relation to Climate-related Risks and Opportunities

Financial Institutions must report on their current governance structures, risk management processes, and strategic frameworks,
specifically as they relate to climate-related risks and opportunities, in accordance with IFRS S2. This reporting will cover how climate-
related risks and opportunities are currently integrated into the reporting entity's decision-making processes at the board and senior
management levels and whether climate-related risks and opportunities are actively being considered within the reporting entity's overall
risk management and strategic planning, be it in the short-, medium-, or long-term periods. Financial Institutions will need to apply the
specific requirements of IFRS S2 to demonstrate the degree to which climate-related risks and opportunities are governed, monitored, and
incorporated into long-term business strategy.

Financial Institutions must acknowledge in their governance, strategy, and risk management disclosures where material climate-related
risks and opportunities are not yet fully subject to formal governance, risk management, or strategic oversight. For instance, some climate
risks may not yet be incorporated into the reporting entity's risk management frameworks, both for enterprise-level and portfolio-level risk
analysis, or the board may not have established a formal process for addressing climate-related risks and opportunities. These disclosures
are expected to include a plan for integrating these items into governance, risk, and strategy considerations in future phases of IFRS S2
implementation if such a plan exists. However, these disclosures do not in themselves require a change to the governance, risk and
strategies of the Reporting Financial Institution.

A Financial Institution does not need to make the quantitative anticipated financial effects disclosures required by IFRS S2, paragraph 9(d)
and IFRS S2, paragraph 16(d). However, they should make the quantitative current period financial effects disclosures specified in
paragraph 9(d), and they must disclose qualitative information on their progress in determining the quantitative anticipated financial effects

disclosures specified in paragraphs 9(d) and 16(d).

Financial Institutions need not use climate-related scenario analysis to assess their climate resilience or the potential financial impact of
climate-related risks and opportunities on their reporting entity. However, they should provide qualitative information on progress in
understanding their climate resilience.

Report on Metrics Related to Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG Emissions

Financial Institutions are required to report on their Scope 1 (direct emissions from owned or controlled sources) and Scope 2 (indirect
emissions from the generation of purchased energy) GHG emissions. The reporting must comply with the metrics outlined in IFRS S2.
Financial Institutions must provide a clear account of the methodologies used to calculate emissions, ensuring transparency and
consistency in line with IFRS S2. Scope 3 emissions (value chain emissions, including Scope 3 operational emissions and financed
emissions) are not required at Implementation Phase 1 (although a Financial Institution may choose to make these disclosures).

Report on Other In-Company Metrics and Targets as Required by IFRS S2

Financial Institutions must, as specified in IFRS S2, disclose information relevant to the cross-industry metric categories, industry-based
metrics and targets set by the reporting entity. However, Implementation Phase 1 does not require reporting on metrics, either qualitative
or quantitative, tied to or incorporated within the reporting entity's value chain (like Scope 3 emissions) or other external parties, allowing
Financial Institutions to focus on internal operations first. Nonetheless, a Financial Institution must apply IFRS S2 requirements to report
on all internal and regulatory imposed reporting entity metrics and targets related to climate-related risks and opportunities, such as for
reducing energy usage, waste management, and internal sustainability initiatives. Thus providing stakeholders with a clear understanding
of the reporting entity’s climate goals and progress toward meeting them. The methodology to estimate and track the metrics and their
progress should remain consistent to aid comparability, and any data-related assumptions that are applied towards metrics and targets

should be suitably disclosed.

Application of IFRS S1 Components to Support IFRS S2 Compliance

Financial Institutions are required to apply relevant components of IFRS S1 that are necessary for compliance with IFRS S2. IFRS S1 focuses
on sustainability-related financial disclosures, and certain provisions, such as the general principles support the disclosure of climate-
related disclosures in line with IFRS S2.

IFRS S1 Materiality relief

When reporting in accordance with IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, an entity's is required to report on those disclosure items that are
financially material. An item is financially material if “omitting, misstating or obscuring? that information could reasonably be expected to influence
decisions that primary users of general purpose financial reports make on the basis of those reports, which include financial statements and
sustainability-related financial disclosures and which provide information about a specific reporting entity.”
Applying this requirement in IFRS S1, a reporting entity is not permitted to:

(a) Omit material information;

(b) Misstate material information, or

(c) Obscure material information
The relief provided effects on the (c) above (in other words, an entity is still prohibited from omitting or misstating material information).

Obscuring material information

When a reporting entity discloses information required by an IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard in the same location as information
disclosed to meet other requirements, including information required by regulators, the reporting entity must ensure that the climate-
related financial disclosures are clearly identifiable and not obscured by that additional information.? Information is obscured if it is

communicated in a way that would have a similar effect for primary users to omitting or misstating that information.*

? Obscuring means that financially material information cannot be ‘hidden’ by, or ‘lost among’ non-material information.

Applying this relief means that reporting entities do not need to assess whether climate-related items are below the threshold for financial
materiality (for example., they may in Implementation Phase 1 include items that might not reasonably be expected to affect the reporting
entity’s prospects). This provides Financial Institutions with some relief from performing the financial materiality test.

Omitting or misstating information

Financial Institutions that apply this relief must publish all financially material information, specified in these guidelines (are not permitted to omit

material information), and must ensure that information is materially correct (are not permitted to misstate information).

IFRS S1 Comparative information relief
Notwithstanding the above, Financial Institutions are not required to disclose comparative information in Implementation Phase 1.

IFRS S1 Fair presentation relief

Notwithstanding the above, in presenting Implementation Phase 1 disclosures, a Financial Institution complying with the aspects of IFRS S1

and IFRS S2 as specified in these guidelines, is presumed to result in climate-related financial disclosures that achieve fair presentation.

(3) This phased approach to IFRS S2 adoption is intended to enable Financial Institutions to
gradually build their capacity for more detailed and comprehensive climate-related
disclosures. The flexibility offered allows Financial Institutions to begin reporting even
when certain data or processes may not yet be fully in place, fostering a culture of
transparency and continuous improvement. By focusing initially on governance, internal
metrics, and Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, Financial Institutions will establish a solid
foundation for managing climate risks, aligned with Rwanda’s broader sustainability goals
and international reporting standards.
